title: fix(console): mint a sys_file id for files picked in the global action dialogs
body:
Fixes #10131

`Clause-②: no` — no exported symbol is added, removed or renamed, no accept set moves, and no key on a published payload changes. This package's published barrel is `plugin.ts` (`ConsolePlugin`, `staticPath`), which this diff does not touch; the `App` and `AppContent` exports of the SPA source keep their names and types. What moves is WHERE a provider is mounted inside the console's own React tree. (The claim comment deliberately carried no `Clause-②:` line — it is declared here, from the diff.)

## Step 1, answered: the mint path exists, and the widget already calls it

- **The file control is `FileField`** in `@object-ui/fields` (with its grid-cell sibling `FileCell`), reached from `field-type-alias`'s `file` entry. It is not the `file-upload` registry component in `@object-ui/components`, which is a designer demo widget.
- **This repo does mint a `sys_file`**: `createObjectStackUploadAdapter` in `@object-ui/providers` runs the server's three-step protocol (presign, PUT, complete) and returns the minted id as `meta.fileId`.
- **The server offers it**: `@objectstack/service-storage` mounts `POST /api/v1/storage/upload/presigned` and `POST /api/v1/storage/upload/complete`, and its route ledger names them as the SDK upload path. Outcome 2 is ruled out.
- **`FileField` already calls that path** through `useUpload()`, and `fileValueForSubmit` already stores the bare id when the adapter surfaced one. Measured on a pre-fix tree, driving the real widget: with a provider whose adapter mints an id, `onChange` receives the **string** `f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f`; with no provider, zero fetches and `onChange` receives `{name, original_name, size, mime_type, url: "blob:…"}`.

So neither half of the card was a missing client. **This is outcome 1, and the thing that was not wired up is the provider's ALTITUDE.**

## The defect

`ConnectedShell`'s `GlobalActionRuntimeProvider` renders `{children}` and then `{runtime.dialogs}` + `{modalElement}` as its **siblings**. The action-param dialog and the `ModalForm` a modal action opens — a lookup's inline "create the referenced record", a related list's New — are therefore mounted **beside** the route element, not under it.

`UploadProvider` was mounted inside `AppContent`, which is the element of exactly one route, `/apps/:appName/*`. Every one of those dialogs rendered outside it.

And `useUpload()` **fails open**: with no provider above it, it silently returns `createObjectUrlAdapter()`, which mints a `blob:` URL locally and reports success. That is both halves of the card in one mount point:

- **no request is ever sent** — the fallback never touches the network, which is why a real `filechooser` produced zero requests on the wire;
- **an object reaches the engine** — with no `meta.fileId`, `fileValueForSubmit` falls back to the legacy inline blob, and the engine answers `expected string, received object`.

The 400 names the payload while the upload is what is missing, exactly as the card says.

## The lit control

A lookup in that same dialog round-trips its opaque server-minted id, and the difference is not the widget layer — it is one provider's altitude. The `dataSource` a lookup needs was **deliberately hoisted** to that level; `GlobalActionRuntimeProvider`'s own docstring says it sits there "so it reaches EVERY field widget, including a relation field inside a create/edit form that renders in a Radix Dialog portal (which sits above the lower per-view ActionProviders)". `SchemaRendererProvider` and the action runtime got that treatment. `UploadProvider` did not.

The second half of the contrast is the failure mode. When a lookup has no data source it renders an explicit empty state — `OptionsEmptyState` has a no-provider case of its own. `useUpload()` has no such state: it fabricates an adapter that reports success. That is why this stayed invisible until a record was saved.

## The fix

One `UploadProvider`, mounted in `App` above `ConsoleShell`, so every console surface shares one upload destination — the app routes, the global dialogs, the two form routes and the organization settings page alike. `AppContent`'s copy is removed, so there is exactly one in the tree.

It is built with `createAuthenticatedFetch`. That is not decoration: `RecordAttachmentsPanel` — the one console surface that was already uploading correctly — states the requirement, that "the storage routes require a session and there is no cookie for `credentials: 'include'` to carry", and `AppContent`'s own `/me/permissions` comment records the same session shape ("with the cookie-only default fetch, a token-only session resolved as anonymous"). The same wrapper also carries `X-Tenant-ID`, so an upload lands in the tenant the rest of the session is reading. Shipping the hoist with the adapter's bare default `fetch` would have moved the failure from "no request" to "401", which reads like progress and is not.

## In-flight and failure behaviour — decided, and pinned as the decision

The card asks for this to be decided rather than inherited, so: **the control holds the field value unchanged until the upload settles, and on failure never writes to it at all.**

- **In flight**: `useFileUploads` calls `onChange` only after the adapter resolves, and `useUploadingSignal` reports the transition to the host. So the value never holds a half-uploaded thing, and a host that must block Submit can — `ActionParamDialog` already does.
- **On failure**: `onChange` is not called, an inline error is rendered, and the field keeps what it had. For a new record with a required `file` that is empty, so the form's own required validation refuses the submit.

This is the choice because it is the only one that avoids both hazards the card names: it never submits a stale id (the value is not touched) and it never submits nothing silently (there is an on-screen error, and required validation still refuses).

## Reverse verification

The fix was committed first, then both source files were restored to the branch base and the pin re-run. The mutation is proved on disk rather than by an exit code: `UploadProvider` occurrences in `App.tsx` went 3 to 0 and in `AppContent.tsx` 0 to 3, and both blob hashes differed from their HEAD blobs.

```
ABLATION_VITEST_EXIT=1
  × reaches a file control mounted beside the route element, and submits the id STRING
      AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
  × builds that adapter with an authenticated fetch, not the bare default
      AssertionError: expected 'undefined' to be 'function'
  Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

The two that stayed green are the counter-probes, and that is the expected direction: the defect-signature probe (no provider anywhere) and the no-file-field control must **not** flip, or the red would be about the harness rather than the altitude. Restore was verified by blob-hash equality against HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by the restore command's exit code.

## Checks

All from the repo root, on the merged tree.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `vitest run --project @object-ui/console` (under the shared verify lock) | 105 files, 1181 tests passed; lock `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/console` (under the lock) | 36/36 tasks successful. `--listFiles` confirms the new pin file is inside the program, so the typecheck really covers it |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint` | exit 0, 0 errors (212 pre-existing warnings). No type-aware linting is configured, so this diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict |
| `check:eager-closure` (after a real `@object-ui/console` build) | green — aggregate and all four per-chunk ceilings. No ceiling was touched, and none needed to be: both newly-written specifiers were already eagerly reachable through `AppContent` |
| `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` | all exit 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the four changed paths | `NOT GOVERNED` — ordinary review and merge-queue route |

## Acceptance notes

Found while establishing the above. None is in this diff.

**To file (reproducible defects):**

1. **A record form can be submitted while an upload is still in flight.** `onUploadingChange` has exactly one consumer, `ActionParamDialog`. The record-form chain in `@object-ui/plugin-form` does not read it, so a user who picks a file and hits Save immediately saves the record without the attachment. Dedupe words: onUploadingChange, ObjectForm, submit, in-flight, upload. Not touched here because those files were declared hands-off for this round.
2. **A `file` field on a FormView renders as a plain text box.** The `/f/:slug` and `/forms/:name` routes go through `FormPage`, which is this repo's second form renderer and has its own hand-rolled input switch with no `file` arm, so a file field falls through to the default text input. Same shape as the lookup sibling that landed as PR objectui#10158, on the other renderer. Dedupe words: FormPage, FormView, file, text input, second renderer.
3. **Every third-party host has the defect this PR repairs, and the console's own fix does not reach them.** `AppContent`'s docstring points hosts that do not want the console's system routes at `DefaultAppContent`, and neither it nor `ConnectedShell` mounts an `UploadProvider` — so such a host gets the same silent object-URL fallback in the same dialogs. Whether app-shell should carry a default upload destination is a contract question, not a repair. Dedupe words: DefaultAppContent, UploadProvider, third-party host, ConnectedShell, upload destination.

**Noted, not filed:** `useUpload`'s fail-open fallback is what made all of the above silent — a deployment with no upload destination is reported to the widget as a successful upload. Making it observable is a contract change to a published hook with existing callers (`ProfilePage`, the organization `SettingsPage`), so it belongs to whoever owns that contract rather than to this card. Successor: the third-party-host card above is the one that has to answer it.
